Mathew (28 Nov 2025, 2025 INSC 1364) exists, but the guide overstates its scope: the registered sale deed in that case (28 June 2004) was executed before the suit was even filed (18 December 2004), well before the attachment (13 Feb 2005). The Court's holding is tied to a pre-suit transfer, not simply any transfer 'before the attachment' as the guide states; a transfer made after suit filing but before attachment raises a separate lis pendens question the ruling does not resolve the same way.

fixes.replace: holding that an attachment before judgment under Order XXXVIII Rule 5 cannot be extended to reach property that was already conveyed to a third party by a registered sale deed executed before the suit was even filed, where that third party's rights were acquired independently of the dispute between the original parties. The ruling does not resolve what happens where the transfer occurs after the suit is filed but before the attachment order itself, a scenario the lis pendens doctrine under Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act may separately affect.
fixes.reason: In L.K. Prabhu, the sale deed was executed before the suit was even filed, not merely before the attachment order; the guide's broader framing ('before the attachment') overstates the protection to cover post-suit, pre-attachment transfers that the ruling did not address.

fixes.replace: It depends on when the transfer happened. The Supreme Court's 2025 ruling in L.K. Prabhu v. K.T.
